row.scim_plan: All Tableau Cloud plans (SAML/OIDC/Google SSO prereq)
row.evidence: Tableau Cloud Help says Tableau Cloud supports SCIM for IdPs once the site is configured for SAML or OIDC (or Google) SSO, with no edition restriction; Salesforce lists Viewer at $15, Explorer $42 and Creator $75 per user/month billed annually.
row.notes: Unchanged from June: SCIM is documented for any Tableau Cloud site with SAML, OIDC or Google SSO; neither the help docs nor Salesforce's Tableau pricing page tie it to an edition. tableau.com/pricing returns Access Denied to automated requests, so prices come from salesforce.com (Creator $75, Explorer $42, Viewer $15 per user/month billed annually; Tableau Cloud from $15). Edition (Standard/Enterprise/Tableau+) gating could not be checked on tableau.com. Deprovisioning sets users to Unlicensed; deletion is manual or via SCIM DELETE only if the user owns no content. Since December 2025 a public Tableau SCIM API (scim.online.tableau.com) is documented. Multiplier 1.0 because SCIM rides on the Viewer licence.

plans.name: Tableau Viewer
plans.notes: Licence role, not a tier; SSO/SCIM are site-level capabilities documented for Tableau Cloud with no edition restriction.

auth.token_source: Settings > Authentication > SCIM > New Configuration > New Secret (site administrator); or an external JWT from a Tableau connected app
auth.notes: The secret becomes invalid if the creating site admin's role changes or they leave the site.

deprovision.data_retained: User is set to the Unlicensed site role and kept with their content; deletion requires the user to own no content (otherwise SCIM DELETE also just sets Unlicensed).
deprovision.notes: action 'other' = licence removed (site role Unlicensed). frees_seat true because Unlicensed users do not hold a licence (active=false means unlicensed).

custom.how: Tableau extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:tableau:3.0 with siteRoles; other attributes are ignored.

roles.how: Site role via the Tableau extension siteRoles or entitlements value (Creator, Explorer, ExplorerCanPublish, SiteAdministratorExplorer, SiteAdministratorCreator, Viewer, Unlicensed); IdP group assignments map to site roles, most permissive wins.

limitations.text: Okta does not sync first and last name to Tableau Cloud on user creation.
User Name and Primary email cannot be updated via Okta SCIM; remove and re-add the user.
A separate Okta app is needed per Tableau Cloud site.
Deprovisioning only sets Unlicensed; users who own content must have ownership reassigned before manual deletion.
SCIM token is tied to the site admin who created the configuration.

capabilities.notes: Licences in Tableau are site roles, so assign_roles/assign_licenses/deactivate (set Unlicensed) all go through Update User's siteRole.

endpoints.purpose: Get users on site (filter, sort, paging)
Update user (site role on Tableau Cloud)
Import users to site from CSV
Delete users from site with CSV

limitations.text: On Tableau Cloud the REST API cannot change a user's password, user name (email) or full name.

okta.notes: OIN page markup marks SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push and Group Linking as checked.

google.notes: SCIM can be tied to Google authentication, but no Google Workspace provisioning app for Tableau was verified.

onelogin.notes: From Tableau's own OneLogin SCIM guide; OneLogin connector page not loaded.

fallbacks.notes: REST API and site UI support CSV import of users; Grant License on Sign In exists for groups.

citations.title: SCIM - Tableau
citations.quote: Tableau Cloud supports SCIM, enabling identity providers (IdPs) to centrally manage user identities while streamlining the process of managing users and group membership in Tableau Cloud.

citations.title: SCIM - Tableau
citations.quote: Your site is already configured to support SAML or OIDC (or Google) single sign-on (SSO).

citations.title: SCIM - Tableau
citations.quote: You can get IdP-specific configuration steps for the following IdPs we support: Configure SCIM with Microsoft Entra ID Configure SCIM with Okta Configure SCIM with OneLogin Configure SCIM with PingFederate

citations.title: SCIM - Tableau
citations.quote: The secret is tied to the Tableau site administrator user who created the SCIM configuration. If that user's site role changes or the user is no longer a member of the site, the secret becomes invalid.

citations.title: SCIM - Tableau
citations.quote: You can bypass the SCIM token that Tableau generates and instead use an externally generated JWT (using a Tableau connected app) to support SCIM requests in Tableau Cloud.

citations.title: SCIM - Tableau
citations.quote: Sign in to your Tableau Cloud site as a site administrator, and select Settings > Authentication .
